subject: Next steps: VPC endpoint & egress checklist for CloudScale integration
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Quick sync recap + network ask

Hi Maria — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single action list to hand to your infra team. High-level ask: we want to make the initial integration low-friction while meeting CloudScale's networking and compliance constraints.

Recap from our call:
- Use case: low-latency user-facing embeddings + reranker for semantic search; occasional higher-throughput batch re-embedding jobs.
- Expected QPS: ~25 requests/sec peak; typical prompt lengths 150-400 tokens.
- Security: SOC2+customers in EU; prefer private connectivity for production.

Redwood recommended approach (initial):
1) Private connectivity: create an AWS PrivateLink (VPC endpoint service) from CloudScale VPC to Redwood Dedicated endpoint in us-west-2. PrivateLink gives stable internal DNS + avoids public egress.
2) Fallback: IP allowlist for our public API IPs (we'll provide ranges) to use briefly during POC.
3) Egress / NAT: if you route traffic through a central NAT egress, ensure 443 outbound to our endpoint(s) allowed.
4) DNS: we will provide private hosted zone names (svc.redwood-inference.internal) to resolve the endpoint inside your VPC; confirm if you want us to create the zone or if you prefer to manage records.
5) mTLS: recommend mTLS on the private endpoint for mutual auth; alternative is short-lived OAuth tokens if mTLS management is a blocker.
6) SDK/auth: Redwood SDK supports both API key (short-lived token exchange) and mTLS client certs. For production we prefer short-lived tokens issued by our token service bound to the PrivateLink connection.
7) Structured output & tool-calling: we’ll enable structured output feature flag on the model route — requires no extra networking, but you may need to open WebSocket/streaming ports for streaming responses if you use that.
8) Embeddings/reranker: typical pattern is embeddings at ingest → vector store in your VPC (hosted or managed) → cross-encoder reranker hosted at Redwood for fast re-rank. We can also run a reranker in your VPC if you need full data residency.

Action items (proposal):
- CloudScale infra to confirm: PrivateLink allowed? (yes/no)
- Provide primary CIDR for endpoint peering and firewall admin contact.
- Confirm whether CloudScale will manage certs for mTLS or prefer Redwood-managed certs.
- We'll send IP ranges, sample terraform snippets, and an initial mutual action plan spreadsheet.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf (quickstart + sample token exchange), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (proposed timeline & owners).

Proposed timeline:
- POC network setup: 2 weeks after confirmation
- Integration & validation (SDK + tool-calls): 1 week
- Canaries + perf validation: 1 week

Next steps: can you introduce your networking lead / SCCM contact and confirm whether PrivateLink is acceptable? If PrivateLink is not possible, we’ll pivot to IP allowlist + TLS.

Thanks — looping in Karthik from Solutions to pick this up on the technical details.

Cheers,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
D: (415) 555-0134 | dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

> Hi Maria — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single action list to hand to your infra team...

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria@cloudscale.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Feb 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RE: Quick sync recap + network ask — technical notes

Maria / Ben — thanks for the diagram and timeline. Karthik will own the technical handoff. A few concrete items and snippets below to help your infra team move quickly.

Short answers up front: PrivateLink + mTLS is our recommended production approach. We'll provide terraform + sample certs for POC. If you want Redwood-managed certs we can provision them and rotate automatically (we support integration with your KMS/HSM).

Technical checklist for CloudScale infra:
- PrivateLink setup: create an Interface VPC Endpoint in your VPC that connects to the Redwood Endpoint Service. We'll provide the Service Name and expected acceptance rule (account ID).
- DNS: create private hosted zone (example: svc.redwood-inference.internal) and an A/CNAME mapping to the interface endpoint ENIs. If using Route 53 Resolver, we can supply zone file.
- IP ranges / port requirements: outbound TCP 443. For fallback public endpoints, allow these CIDR blocks: 34.201.0.0/18, 52.23.128.0/18 (we'll give the authoritative list in the SPA).
- mTLS options:
  * Option A (recommended): client cert + server cert mutual TLS on PrivateLink. We can supply client certs and rotate via automation or accept your certs.
  * Option B: OAuth2 client_credentials + short-lived tokens (recommended for SDK clients that do not manage certs).
- SDK auth sample: see attached quickstart (redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf) — sample flow uses token exchange:
  1) App authenticates to CloudScale IdP → obtains federated token or uses service account.
  2) App calls token-exchange endpoint at Redwood with proof-of-possession bound to VPC endpoint.
  3) Redwood returns short-lived bearer token (TTL 1h) used by SDK.
- Egress considerations: If you SNAT traffic at a central NAT, ensure sticky source IPs for the PrivateLink activation step (we'll accept the endpoint from your account).
- Structured output / tool calling: enable structured_output flag for the route; streaming works over the same TLS channel. If you need network policies to allow long-lived streams, ensure your LB or proxies don’t terminate idle streams under 60s.
- Embeddings + rerank: recommend embedding vectors be stored in your VPC-managed vector DB (no egress if you host it); for the reranker we can host the cross-encoder in Redwood and call it over the PrivateLink. If you prefer, we can containerize reranker and run it in your VPC private subnet.

I'll attach a small terraform snippet and a sample acceptance rule. Also attaching a one-tab mutual-action-plan.xlsx with owners and dates.

Karthik — can you propose the minimal acceptance rule and the sample Route 53 entries we should send to CloudScale?

Thanks,
Dylan

---
Attachment references: redwood-sdk-quickstart.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Re: RE: Quick sync recap + network ask — acceptance rules & sample records

Hi Maria / Ben — quick technical follow-up with the exact items our infra will need to complete the PrivateLink acceptance and route traffic.

1) Endpoint acceptance rule
- Accept connections from account: 987654321012 (Redwood service account). Please add that account ID when you create the VPC endpoint service acceptance.

2) Route 53 private hosted zone
- Zone name: svc.redwood-inference.internal
- Records to create (example):
  * model-api.svc.redwood-inference.internal CNAME -> vpce-0a1b2c3d4e-abcdef.elb.amazonaws.com
  * embeddings.svc.redwood-inference.internal CNAME -> vpce-0a1b2c3d4e-emb.elb.amazonaws.com

3) Ports / timeouts
- Outbound: TCP 443 only. No other ports required.
- Keep-alive: set idle timeout >= 90s for streaming scenarios.

4) mTLS certs
- If CloudScale manages your client certs: we'll provide CSR & expected SAN entries.
- If Redwood manages certs: we will provision and rotate and publish rotation events to your PagerDuty webhook.

5) CIDR recommendations for private endpoints (suggested subnets): 10.10.240.0/24 (interface endpoints).

6) Terraform snippet (pseudo):
- Provide minimal snippet in the shared Drive doc; we'll paste exact code there.

Ben: if you can confirm the VPC id and an owner email for acceptance, we'll create the endpoint service on our side and share the ServiceName. After you accept, we can start end-to-end tests (token exchange + sample structured output call).

Thanks — I’ll be available Mon for a quick run-through.

Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
